parts.problem_md:
Study the photograph of a coastal landscape.

![Rocky coastal landscape with small sandy beaches, sea, and grassy cliffs under a cloudy sky. A kayak is visible on the left shore.](assets/001-rocky-coastal-landscape-with-small-sandy-beaches.png)

Identify the main process and its features that helped shape the coastline.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> The cliff shows signs of erosion from waves** [1]**, creating a headland [**1]**, with possibly three small bays **[1]** and a wave-cut platform **[1]**.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** for identification of erosion as the main physical process.
> - 3 @ 1 mark **[1]** for identifying features.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> - Small amounts of sand in bays, providing the answer is linked to erosion and not deposition (attrition).

parts.problem_md: Explain how GIS can help decision-makers reduce the impacts of flooding.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> GIS can show which areas are at greatest risk [**1]**, so evacuation plans can be made [**1]**. It can also help to plan where to build defences [**1]** or prevent housing from being developed in dangerous areas. [**1] **This reduces loss of life and property [**1]**.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** for each valid point up to a maximum of 5 marks.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Think 'information → decision → outcome'.

parts.problem_md: A flood risk map shows red zones near rivers and green zones on higher land. Which zone is safer for a hospital and why?
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> The green zone is safer, as it avoids flood damage. **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 4.2, which shows an area of Brazil that has been partially deforested.

![Tall trees with sparse foliage stand over a grassy field with grazing cattle, set against a hazy sky, depicting deforestation impacts.](assets/002-tall-trees-with-sparse-foliage-stand-over-a-gras.png)

*Fig. 4.2 *

Describe the vegetation shown in Fig. 4.2.
parts.solution_md:
The image shows tall, dispersed palm trees** **with straight, thin, branchless trunks. **[1]** Some of the trees appear to be dead and burnt. **[1] **The grass appears dry and yellow** [1],**** **with scattered ferns and shrubs throughout. **[1] **

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - One mark **[1]** for each valid observation
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> - Coconut trees **[1 mark].**
> - Isolated/separated/scattered/sparse/spread **[1 mark].**
> - Leaves/branches at top **[1 mark].**
> - Some trees don’t have leaves/are stripped of leaves/have dying leaves or palms **[1 mark].**
> - Some trunks are cut off/stumps/lower parts remain **[1 mark].**
> - Grass brown/dried (grass) **[1 mark].**
> - Bushes **[1 mark].**

parts.problem_md:
Study Figs. 6.2, 6.3 and 6.4, which are photographs of economic activities that increase greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

![Power station, grazing cattle and deforestation](assets/003-power-station-grazing-cattle-and-deforestation.png)

*Figs. 6.2, 3 and 4*

Explain how each of the economic activities shown in Figs. 6.2, 6.3 and 6.4 increases greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Fig. 6.2 is a power station that gives off/emits/produces carbon dioxide.
> 
> Fig. 6.3 shows grazing cattle that give off/emit/produce methane.
> 
> Fig. 6.4 shows deforestation that results in less carbon dioxide (CO₂) being absorbed/removed or converted to oxygen **OR**
> 
> Fig. 6.4 shows vehicles that give off/emit/produce carbon dioxide (CO₂)/carbon monoxide (CO)/sulphur dioxide/nitrogen/nitrous oxides.

parts.problem_md:
![A small river meanders through a grassy landscape with trees in the background, under an overcast sky. Eroded banks and patches of reeds are visible.](assets/004-a-small-river-meanders-through-a-grassy-landscap.png)

*Fig. 4.1*

What river feature is shown in Fig. 4.1?
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **B** is the correct answer.** [1 mark]**
> 
> The other answers are incorrect because:
> 
> **A: **The confluence is where two river channels merge.
> 
> **C: **An oxbow is a meander loop that has been cut off, leaving behind a small lake.
> 
> **D:** The source is where a river begins.
